name: Alpha-GPC

lead: Alpha-GPC is a choline-containing compound sold as a supplement, and as a prescription drug for cognitive decline in Italy. Lifters take it for focus and training output, hoping for harder sessions that support muscle gain.

It supplies choline, a precursor of acetylcholine and of membrane phospholipids, and rat studies reported raised hippocampal acetylcholine. Most human research is older Italian multicentre work in stroke, transient ischaemic attacks and dementia, with newer registered trials in cognition and athletic performance in healthy adults. One 2024 trial lists growth hormone as an outcome. No study has tested appearance outcomes.

paras: It is taken orally as a supplement, commonly before training or as part of a nootropic routine.
Older Italian trials reported low adverse event rates; detailed safety data are limited. It is sold as a supplement in the US and is not FDA-approved as a drug.

angle.text: Alpha-GPC is a choline source that lifters take for focus and training output, aiming at harder sessions that support muscle gain. It is a prescription drug for cognitive decline in Italy.

lead: Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, or choline alfoscerate) is a choline-containing compound that serves as a source of choline for the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine and for cell membrane phospholipids [1]. According to Grokipedia, it is a prescription drug in some countries such as Italy for cognitive decline and is sold as a dietary supplement in the United States, where a 2012 GRAS notice addressed its use as a choline source [1].

Most published human research dates from Italian multicentre studies in the 1990s in stroke, transient ischaemic attacks and dementia [2][3][4]. More recent registered trials have examined it for cognition and athletic performance in healthy adults [5][6][7][8].
No published study has tested alpha-GPC for facial or body appearance outcomes, and the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing forum discussion of it.
infobox: Dietary supplement; not FDA-approved as a drug [1]

paras: Rat studies in the early 1990s reported that oral alpha-GPC reversed scopolamine-induced amnesia and increased hippocampal acetylcholine synthesis and release [9][10]. Another rat study examined molecular mechanisms in young and aged animals, and a pharmacokinetic study tracked radiolabelled alpha-GPC in rats [11][12]. In healthy volunteers, a comparison of free plasma choline after intramuscular alpha-GPC and citicoline was published in 1992 [13].

Grokipedia attributes the first preparation to Erich Baer and Marvin Kates in 1948 and the first commercial availability to Italfarmaco in Italy in 1987 as a treatment for cognitive disorders, followed by supplement sales in the US from the 1990s and later sports-nutrition use [1].

An open Italian multicentre trial of 2,044 patients with recent stroke or transient ischaemic attack followed mental recovery with alpha-GPC, given by injection and then orally [2]. A randomised multicentre study of 126 patients with probable Alzheimer-type dementia compared alpha-GPC with acetyl-L-carnitine and reported improvements in most neuropsychological measures in alpha-GPC recipients [3]. A multicentre trial in vascular dementia compared alpha-GPC with cytosine diphosphocholine [4].

Registered trials in healthy adults have examined effects on muscle power, growth hormone and cognition, on physical and cognitive performance in volleyball players, and on cognitive performance and sports performance in young adults [5][6][7][8][14]. A growth-hormone outcome is relevant to height-related community interest, but the results are not given in the sources reviewed. No studies were found testing alpha-GPC for appearance outcomes.
Grokipedia describes alpha-GPC as sold over the counter in the US and included in sports-nutrition products [1]. The sources reviewed contain no discussion of it in looksmaxxing forums.

timeline.event: First prepared by Baer and Kates, per Grokipedia [1].
Launched in Italy by Italfarmaco, per Grokipedia [1].
